nodes.name: definitions.ts
nodes.summary: Fetches Autobrr indexer definitions from GitHub API at startup and every 24h with jitter, caches normalized definition names in a Set for detecting autobrrMissing indexers
nodes.languageNotes: TypeScript module using axios for HTTP to GitHub API, crypto for UUID logger correlation, Set-based in-memory cache, 3 retry attempts with exponential backoff capped at 10s, recursive setTimeout with 20% jitter for periodic refresh

nodes.name: indexer-fetcher.ts
nodes.summary: Fetches indexer data from Prowlarr API and IRC network data from Autobrr API with retry logic, circuit breakers, channel alias resolution, and reachability flags
nodes.languageNotes: TypeScript module with axios HTTP client, circuit breaker pattern per service (3 failures triggers 60s jittered cooldown), exponential backoff retry (1 retry per upstream call), reachability flags for service status tracking, channel alias mapping (mtv/morethantv, td/torrentday, tl/torrentleech) for indexer name matching

nodes.name: indexer-history.ts
nodes.summary: Manages indexer state transition history in SQLite via knex, computes per-source downtime in minutes and 24h time-weighted uptime percentages, performs 14-day cleanup capped at once per 24h
nodes.languageNotes: TypeScript using knex query builder for SQLite, transition-only inserts (only inserts on up/down state change per source to reduce noise), time-weighted uptime percentage from boundary rows spanning the 24h window, per-source tracking (prowlarr/autobrr/qbittorrent) with separate Maps, 14-day cleanup window

nodes.name: indexer-types.ts
nodes.summary: TypeScript type definitions for Indexer, AutobrrStatus, ServiceStatus, and ServiceStatuses used across the indexer monitoring system
nodes.languageNotes: TypeScript interfaces file, imports QbitStatus from qbittorrent and TrackerStats from tracker-stats for composition in the Indexer interface

nodes.name: indexer.ts
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the full indexer fetch cycle: fetches from Prowlarr + Autobrr, merges with qBittorrent + tracker stats, records history + Prometheus metrics, fires alerts, caches icons, and serves cached results with disk-backed stale-while-revalidate
nodes.languageNotes: TypeScript orchestrator module that coordinates 7+ services per poll cycle, disk-backed JSON cache with serialization dedup (writes only on content change), background fetch pattern returning stale cache immediately while fetching fresh data, Prometheus metrics recording per-indexer and per-service, fs-based cache file alongside SQLite DB

nodes.name: qbittorrent.ts
nodes.summary: qBittorrent client with cookie-based auth and 403 re-auth, torrent/tracker polling with domain matching and override aliases, circuit breaker with probe fallback, connection status and port check
nodes.languageNotes: TypeScript module with cookie-based authentication (form POST to /api/v2/auth/login), automatic re-auth on 403 responses, domain suffix matching with override aliases (hd-space.org, rutracker.org, tday.love), batched tracker fetches at 10 concurrent, circuit breaker with probe-only mode on cooldown, background setInterval-style polling with jitter (QBITTORRENT_POLL_INTERVAL_S, default 300s)

nodes.name: tracker-stats.ts
nodes.summary: Fetches per-indexer buffer/ratio stats from UNIT3D tracker APIs using Prowlarr-extracted API keys, with platform detection cache, blacklisting for non-UNIT3D indexers, and periodic refresh
nodes.languageNotes: TypeScript module with dual-layer caching (platformCache to avoid re-probing non-UNIT3D indexers, blacklistedUntil for temporarily failed indexers), handles Prowlarr-masked apiKey values (********), parses byte strings (KiB/MiB/GiB) from UNIT3D API, supports Bearer header and api_token query param auth, SSRF protection via isPrivateUrl

nodes.name: indexer-alerts.ts
nodes.summary: Manages alert state tracking for indexer down events with configurable delay (ALERT_DELAY_M), alerts only on transition to down, persists state to SQLite alert_state table with chunked upserts
nodes.languageNotes: TypeScript module with in-memory Set (alertedDownIds) + Map (downSince) for alert dedup, SQLite persistence via knex alert_state table with onConflict merge, chunked upserts at 300 rows per batch, ALERT_DELAY_M support (delay before firing alert), first-poll recovery loads persisted state

nodes.name: apprise.ts
nodes.summary: Apprise notification dispatch supporting ntfy:// URLs via direct HTTP and all other URLs via bundled apprise-go binary, with exponential backoff retry and Prometheus tracking
nodes.languageNotes: TypeScript module with dual dispatch path (ntfy direct HTTP POST vs apprise-go binary exec), retry with 1s/2s exponential backoff, Promise.allSettled for per-channel independence, ntfy URL parser for custom scheme, Prometheus alertSends counter tracking success/failure per channel

nodes.name: indexer-icons.ts
nodes.summary: Discovers, downloads, and caches favicon icons for each indexer from their site URLs with 24h TTL, magic byte content-type detection, and SSRF protection
nodes.languageNotes: TypeScript module with HTML link rel=icon extraction from indexer homepage, magic byte detection for PNG/ICO/SVG (0x89PNG, 0x00000100 ICO, <svg/<?xml SVGs), file-system cache alongside SQLite DB path, atomic write via .tmp+rename pattern, SSRF protection via isPrivateUrl, 24h TTL with jitter

nodes.name: logger.ts
nodes.summary: Structured JSON logger with log level filtering (debug/info/warn/error), request ID child loggers, and Error stack trace capture
nodes.languageNotes: TypeScript utility, structured JSON logging via console.log/warn/error, child logger factory for request correlation via requestId field, LOG_LEVEL env support, Error stack capture on error level, object spread merge into log entry

nodes.name: metrics.ts
nodes.summary: Prometheus client metric definitions (Counter, Histogram, Gauge) and metrics HTTP handler for the IndexMon dashboard, covering poll cycles, upstream reachability, per-indexer status, and alert sends
nodes.languageNotes: TypeScript using prom-client library, collects default Node.js metrics, exports 8 Gauges, 3 Counters, 1 Histogram for indexer monitoring, provides metricsHandler Express endpoint for /metrics route

tour.title: Architecture Overview — Single Container
tour.description: The README describes a single container running nginx (:80), Express (:3000), and SQLite. The root Dockerfile uses a three-stage multi-stage build: frontend-builder (Vite), backend-builder (tsc), and a lean runtime stage (node:26-alpine + nginx). docker-compose.yml defines a single service that builds from Dockerfile, exposes port 80, mounts /app/data for SQLite persistence, and loads env vars from .env. nginx.conf runs daemon-off to keep the process in foreground, reverse-proxies /api/* to Express on port 3000, and writes JSON-structured access logs to stdout. The docker-entrypoint.sh backgrounds nginx then execs the Express server so both processes share PID 1.

tour.title: Backend Server Bootstrap
tour.description: backend/src/server.ts is the backend entrypoint called from docker-entrypoint.sh via `exec node dist/server.js`. The `startServer` async IIFE generates or loads the admin password hash (random 24-char hex or ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH env), inits the Autobrr definition checker, starts qBittorrent background polling, and launches tracker stats refresh — all before calling app.listen(3000). The `shutdown` closure handles SIGTERM/SIGINT: drains icon caches, closes the HTTP server, stops background timers, destroys knex, and forces exit after 10s. The app is wired together in backend/src/app.ts — the Express instance that registers helmet, cookie-parser, requestId, httpMetrics, then defines inline /health and /metrics endpoints before mounting the auth router (unprotected), then protected indexers and apprise routers behind authMiddleware, finishing with a global error handler.

tour.title: Express Middleware Stack
tour.description: Each request flows through a pipeline of middlewares registered in app.ts. requestIdMiddleware attaches a UUID and a correlated child logger to res.locals for request tracing. httpMetricsMiddleware starts a Prometheus histogram timer recording method/route/status latencies. The auth router mounts rate-limited login before authMiddleware guards the rest. The inline /api/indexers/icon/:prowlarrId handler also sits before auth (so tags can fetch without cookies) with its own 500/15min rate limit. Centralized errorHandler at the end catches any unhandled errors, logs the stack through the correlated logger, and returns a 500 JSON response.

tour.title: Authentication — Cookie-Based Sessions
tour.description: Auth is entirely in-memory — no DB needed. On startup, server.ts sets the bcrypt password hash via `setPasswordHash`. The login handler validates the password with bcrypt.compare, generates a 24-char hex session token via crypto.randomBytes, stores it in an in-memory Map with 24h expiry, and sets an httpOnly SameSite=strict cookie. The authMiddleware validates the session cookie on every protected request (cleaning expired entries lazily). A setInterval every 15min purges stale sessions. The `/api/auth/logout` endpoint deletes the session from the Map. The auth routes define three endpoints: POST /api/auth/login (rate-limited 10/15min), POST /api/auth/logout, and GET /api/auth/me — used by the frontend on mount to verify the session is still valid. Password hash utilities in scripts/ let you generate custom ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH values.

tour.title: Prowlarr & Autobrr Data Fetching
tour.description: The indexer-fetcher service is the data pipeline entry point. On each poll cycle it hits Prowlarr's /api/v1/indexer and /api/v1/health (handling Prowlarr 2.x's dropped `status` field by parsing IndexerStatusCheck health warnings) and Autobrr's /api/irc endpoint. Both paths have per-service circuit breakers: 3 consecutive failures trigger a 60s jittered cooldown. Upstream calls have 10s timeouts with 1 retry (1s→2s backoff). Reachability flags track whether each service responded. Autobrr IRC channel health = `network.connected && channel.monitoring` (channel.enabled is explicitly NOT checked — it's a user preference). Channel aliases map common abbreviations (mtv→morethantv, td→torrentday, tl→torrentleech) for name matching. The definitions service separately fetches known Autobrr indexer definitions from the GitHub API at startup and every 24h (±30min jitter), building a Set for autobrrMissing detection. The normalize utility lowercases, strips (API), and collapses punctuation — critical for cross-source name matching between Prowlarr, Autobrr, and the definitions set.

tour.title: History & Uptime Tracking
tour.description: The indexer-history service records only state transitions (up→down or down→up) per source (prowlarr/autobrr/qbittorrent) to avoid filling the DB with duplicate rows. On each poll cycle, `insertTransitions` queries the latest status per indexer_id+source and only inserts when the status changed. `computeDowntime` calculates how long a currently-down indexer has been down per source by measuring from the most recent down transition. `computeUptime` computes a 24-hour time-weighted uptime percentage using transition edge timestamps plus pre-window boundary rows for accuracy. `attachDowntimeUptime` mutates Indexer objects in-place with the computed metrics. A 14-day cleanup housekeeper runs at most once per 24h. These metrics feed directly into the tile colors (red for Prowlarr-down, orange for qB errors, etc.) and the IndexerTable's duration/uptime tooltips.

tour.title: Alerting & Apprise Notifications
tour.description: The indexer-alerts service manages the lifecycle of down-event notifications. On the first poll after startup, it loads persisted state from the alert_state SQLite table. On subsequent polls, `handlePollAlerts` detects newly-down indexers (across Prowlarr, Autobrr, and qBittorrent sources), tracks `downSince` timestamps for ALERT_DELAY_M support, and fires `sendAlert` for each new down event. Dedup is both in-memory (alertedDownIds Set) and DB-persisted (alert_state table with text PK, chunked upserts at 300 rows/batch). The apprise service dispatches through two paths: ntfy:// URLs go via direct HTTP POST with an Icon header; all other schemes (slack, telegram, etc.) go through the bundled apprise-go binary with --attach for favicon SVGs. Each channel gets up to 3 retries with 1s/2s exponential backoff, independent per-channel via Promise.allSettled. The /api/apprise/test endpoint lets users verify their notification config from the dashboard UI.

tour.title: qBittorrent Polling & Tracker Stats
tour.description: Two background services run independently. The qBittorrent service authenticates via cookie-based form POST to /api/v2/auth/login (auto-re-auth on 403), polls /api/v2/torrents and /api/v2/torrents/trackers at a configurable interval (default 300s), and matches indexers to their tracker statuses using domain suffix matching with DOMAIN_OVERRIDES for aliased domains (hd-space.org, rutracker.org, tday.love). Batched tracker fetches run at 10 concurrent requests. Its own circuit breaker (3 failures → cooldown) prevents hammering a down qB instance. The tracker-stats service fetches per-indexer buffer/ratio stats from UNIT3D API endpoints using API keys extracted from Prowlarr indexer fields. It has a dual-layer cache: platformCache avoids re-probing non-UNIT3D trackers, blacklistedUntil handles temporary failures. Handles Prowlarr-masked apiKey values (********). SSRF protection via isPrivateUrl. Both services start in server.ts and stop on graceful shutdown.

tour.title: Indexer Orchestrator — The Hub
tour.description: The indexer.ts orchestrator ties everything together. The public `fetchIndexers` function implements a stale-while-revalidate pattern: returns cached data (from an in-memory or disk-backed JSON cache) immediately, then triggers a background `doFetch` cycle that updates the cache. A full poll cycle calls the indexer-fetcher for Prowlarr+Autobrr data, merges in qBittorrent status via domain matching, attaches tracker stats from the stats cache, records Prometheus metrics, calls insertTransitions/computeDowntime/computeUptime from the history service, fires alerts via handlePollAlerts, and schedules icon caching. The disk-backed cache serializes to a JSON file alongside the SQLite DB and only writes on actual content changes (serialization dedup). The /api/indexers route calls fetchIndexers and pre-computes the services reachability status map. The /api/indexers/history route provides paginated access to raw transition data.

tour.title: Observability — Logs, Metrics & Health
tour.description: Three pillars of observability. The structured JSON logger (logger.ts) outputs every line as JSON with level, message, timestamp, and optional requestId for correlation. LOG_LEVEL env controls filtering (default info). Child loggers created by requestIdMiddleware propagate the correlation ID through downstream calls. Prometheus metrics are defined in metrics.ts using prom-client: poll duration histogram, poll total counter, upstream reachability gauges per service, circuit breaker open gauges, per-indexer up/down gauges, 24h uptime percentages, announce age seconds, tracker buffer bytes, and HTTP request duration histograms from the httpMetrics middleware. The /metrics endpoint exposes all of these in OpenMetrics format (unauthenticated). The /health endpoint returns { ok: true } for Docker HEALTHCHECK — also unauthenticated.

tour.title: Database Schema & Startup Initialization
tour.description: SQLite via Knex + better-sqlite3. The runtime DB path comes from DB_PATH env (default /app/data/indexmon.db), configured in database.ts with WAL mode and 5000ms busy timeout. Migrations live in backend/migrations/: the initial 20260518 migration created users, sessions, and indexer_history tables; 20260524 added the source column to indexer_history for per-source tracking; 20260527 added the alert_state table for persistent alert dedup; 20260530 dropped users/sessions after auth moved to in-memory Map. The knexfile.ts uses data/db.sqlite for the migration CLI (separate from runtime). The init-db.cjs script runs at container startup via docker-entrypoint.sh, creating the indexer_history and alert_state tables via raw SQL before the server starts — ensuring the DB exists even without running migrations.

tour.title: Frontend Entry & Routing
tour.description: The React SPA entry point is frontend/index.html — an HTML shell with an inline dark-mode detection script (checks localStorage 'dark' then prefers-color-scheme) that sets the 'dark' class on <body> before React even mounts. main.tsx mounts the React root, wrapping the app in QueryClientProvider (TanStack Query), AuthProvider, and ErrorBoundary around RouterProvider. The router (routes.tsx) defines two routes: /login (LoginPage, no auth guard) and / (DashboardPage wrapped in ProtectedRoute, which redirects to /login if unauthenticated). The outer App.tsx renders Outlet + Toaster for notifications. Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui primitives (button, table, toaster, use-toast) provide the UI foundation. The cn utility merges Tailwind classes, and stripApi removes (API) suffixes from indexer names for cleaner display.

tour.title: Frontend Authentication Flow
tour.description: AuthContext provides the authentication state to the entire React tree. On mount, AuthProvider calls GET /api/auth/me to check if an existing session cookie is still valid, setting isAuthenticated accordingly. The login flow: LoginPage renders a password form, calls POST /api/auth/login via the configured Axios instance, and on success updates AuthContext state which triggers a redirect to /. The Axios instance (utils/axios.ts) is configured with withCredentials: true for cookie forwarding, and has a response interceptor that catches 401 responses and auto-redirects to /login. ProtectedRoute wraps the dashboard route, consuming useAuth to check isAuthenticated and redirecting to /login if not, while showing a loading spinner during the initial session validation. The login page has error handling for wrong passwords and network failures, using the toast system for feedback.

tour.title: Dashboard — Polling & Visualization
tour.description: The useIndexers hook uses TanStack Query's useQuery with a 15s refetchInterval to continuously poll GET /api/indexers, with exponential backoff retry on failure. DashboardPage consumes this hook and renders two main sections inside CollapsibleSection panels: the StatusGrid (color-coded overview tiles) and the IndexerTable (detailed status table). The StatusGrid implements the composite 'worst wins' priority logic: red (Prowlarr down) > orange (qB errors) > yellow (Autobrr disconnected) > grey (autobrrMissing) > amber (low buffer ratio) > green (healthy). Tile transitions animate: alert-pulse on entering red/orange, recover on leaving. The IndexerTable shows each indexer with its icon, clickable name linking to the tracker site, Prowlarr/Autobrr/qBittorrent status columns with duration and uptime tooltips, and a buffer column with color-coded ratio display. Dark mode toggles via a button that writes to localStorage and updates the 'dark' class on <html>.

tour.title: Infrastructure & CI/CD
tour.description: The CI/CD pipeline (.github/workflows/ci.yml) has three jobs. lint-test runs on all pushes/PRs to main: backend install → lint → typecheck → test (Jest), frontend install → lint → test (Vitest), then a Docker build (no push). build-and-publish (on push to main + v* tags): buildx multi-arch Docker image, push to ghcr.io with 'develop' tag (main) or semver+'latest' (v* tags). screenshot (on v* tags only): starts the container, runs a Playwright script (scripts/screenshot.mjs) that mocks 10 indexers via route interception, captures desktop (1280×900) and mobile (412×915, Android phone frame) light+dark screenshots, and uploads to the GitHub release. The Playwright script generates inline PNG favicons for mock data using manual CRC-32 + PNG chunk encoding. Dependabot monitors npm, Docker, and GitHub Actions deps.

tour.title: Testing Structure
tour.description: Backend tests (8 Jest files with supertest) cover: auth (login validation, session cookie, me/logout), normalise utility (edge cases, cross-source name matching), apprise (ntfy dispatch, apprise-go binary, retry logic), indexers routing (auth guard, icon path traversal), fetchIndexers service (Prowlarr empty/healthy/down, Autobrr matching, circuit breaker), indexer-alerts (first poll recovery, down detection, dedup, recovery), indexer-fetcher (buildAutobrrMap, aliases, breaker logic), and indexer-history (transition inserts, downtime/uptime computation, 14d cleanup). Tests use real knex/SQLite (default :memory: with DB_PATH=:memory:). Frontend tests (3 Vitest+testing-library files) cover: LoginPage (form rendering, error states, successful login navigation), DashboardPage (loading, error, data rendering, dark mode toggle, test notification), and IndexerTable (cell rendering, durations, buffer display, service columns). matchMedia is mocked in setup-tests.ts.
